BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents against our playbook. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

Prepared for the Wattlebridge deal team. Seller documents treated as the counterparty's draft; assessed against the Buyer Playbook. Note at the outset: no Amelia Frost written approval exists for any fallback, so all fallback positions below are **unavailable** at this stage.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT – hold at 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is our conditional fallback and no Amelia Frost authority identifying this draft has been given, so we cannot accept it.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping basket (liable from first dollar once exceeded).
- **Recommendation:** REJECT – Seller's thresholds are 5x our playbook on both limbs and convert the basket into a deductible, materially eroding recovery.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months (cl 12.3/13), plus a default that any limitation applies to *all* Claims unless stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months; limitations apply only where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT – 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval (none given), and the "applies to all Claims" default is a hidden general-regime override (see N-014).

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum 6 years, outside general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT – collapsing title into the general regime would cap our recovery on a total failure of title at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m purchase; this is a core, non-negotiable position.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5); no fraud carve-out appears anywhere.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT – insert express carve-out; the draft as written purports to limit fraud liability, which no one on our side may waive and which is unlikely to be enforceable in any event.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records (Sch 7; DL [1.1]–[1.2]); [1.4] denies any admission.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT – whole-data-room/public-register disclosure would qualify every warranty by reference to material we have not been told is relevant, defeating the purpose of the warranty package.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never applicable to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT – a "discoverable" standard imputes constructive knowledge of the whole data room and public registers and effectively duplicates the N-006 problem from the other side.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery" of counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL [2] confirms no final written consent and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied; Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue.
- **Buyer wants:** Effective consent **and** evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied as a condition precedent; not consent-on-delivery; endeavours standard insufficient.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT – a 30%-revenue customer's conditional consent cannot be treated as satisfied merely on receipt of paper; the CP must require satisfaction of the conditions before Completion.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL [3] confirms not repaid and no discharge of security in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT – on a debt-free/cash-free deal we would otherwise be paying AUD 24m and acquiring a company still encumbered for AUD 3.2m; require payout letter, direct payment and release deeds at Completion.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL [5] confirms they are absent from the funds flow and silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or expressly Seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT – a Completion-triggered liability sitting in the target with no funding mechanism is a disguised price leak; require line item or Seller funding, with on-costs quantified.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL [4]: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but is not independent verification; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Broadened indemnity covering failure of IP title/transfer and consequential loss arising from the Ironquay matter, while preserving the SOW3 payment cure; treat AUD 180,000 as unverified either way.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT narrow scope – the real risk is non-vesting of Project Materials, not just a AUD 180k payment; broaden indemnity and require either bank evidence of cleared payment plus confirmatory assignment before Completion or an indemnity that covers the IP gap.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller:** DD-006 described as "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL [6]: ~1,240 records sent to unintended external address; unknown whether accessed; notification requirement undetermined; no confirmed breach; no loss amount.
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, investigation to completion, ongoing update obligation to Completion; no assumption of confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any numeric exposure in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** DO NOT ACCEPT the "not material" characterisation; require covenants to preserve logs, complete the investigation, and update us before Completion, with a specific indemnity to be scoped once facts are known – we have no basis yet to quantify or dismiss this.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals (3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs". DL [8] does not state whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Assessment of DD-008/DD-011 together for timing/scope; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** ASSESS, don't concede – request the terms, termination rights and accrual status; neither accept the Seller's "ordinary course" label nor push for a price adjustment until the position is established.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13); "Tax and IP settled under the general regime"; title folded into general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate with their own regimes; no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT – the "unless expressly stated otherwise" default and the Tax/IP sweep-in are a single mechanism to pull every category under the 20%/18-month general cap; delete and build out distinct schedules.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title to 100% evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. DL [10] concedes this only identifies the Seller's source and that Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence (ASIC searches, PPSR, constitution, board/shareholder approvals, Seller capacity).
- **Recommendation:** REJECT reliance on DD-012 alone – it is a Seller-supplied internal document, not independent proof; commission our own searches and require certified copies and capacity/authority deliverables at Completion.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP "settled under the general regime above".
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP remain OPEN; separate regime to be negotiated; no assumption of unlimited liability and no assumption of resolution.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT the assertion that these are settled – record in our mark-up that Tax and IP are expressly reserved and un-agreed, so that silence is not later taken as acceptance of the general cap.

---

## Summary for the deal team

- **Every one of the 16 positions is rejected or held open.** The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced" – it uniformly pushes toward our fallbacks or below them, and layers general disclosure, constructive buyer knowledge, and an all-Claims limitation default so that the warranty package would have little residual value.
- **Approvals check:** The Seller has landed exactly on our two conditional fallbacks (20% cap; 18 months). No Amelia Frost written authority exists for either. Recommend we do not signal flexibility on those points in the mark-up.
- **Completion mechanics gaps (real cash/risk exposure):** Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m unreleased), bonuses (AUD 420k + on-costs unfunded), Bluefen (30% revenue, consent conditions unmet), Ironquay (IP may not vest). These are the priority items for the next call.
- **Facts not yet established (do not quantify either way):** DD-006 incident scope/notification; Ironquay AUD 180k payment status; Sandbar renewal character; Tax/IP regime.
- **Useful admissions in the Disclosure Letter** to cite back: [2] no Bluefen consent/evidence; [3] Riverlark not repaid; [5] bonuses absent from funds flow; [10] Buyer has not verified title. These undercut the Seller Update's "addressed"/"adequate"/"evidenced" language.

Happy to turn this into a clause-by-clause mark-up of the SPA or a short issues-list email to Seller counsel.
